advantages.what: Ships a README that accurately tells the requester the id rules, member rules, error statuses, persistence and concurrency guarantees; Z delivers no customer-facing document, so nothing is told
A DATA_FILE holding valid JSON without a groups array is refused rather than silently treated as empty and overwritten
A DATA_FILE in a missing directory fails at startup; Z starts and answers 500 to every write
Group ids capped at 16 KiB with header budget derived from saved ids, so every 201 group stays addressable
Tests cover failed ledger writes, creation race and restart numbering more widely, though some pin Y's own layout and rename mechanism and the unknown-split check goes untested
Unknown-split check is actually guarded by its tests; in Y dropping it passes the suite
Leaner product: no shipped acceptance scripts and no stale Open points or duplicated headings in the spec for a maintainer to carry
Concurrency rests on an explicit single write queue; Z's safety depends on there being no await in the expense route, easy to break silently

lesser_lacks: Write a README describing the routes, validation rules, error statuses, id handling and persistence guarantees
Refuse to start (or keep the file aside) when DATA_FILE is valid JSON without a groups array
Fail at startup when DATA_FILE's parent directory does not exist instead of answering 500 to every write
pairs.why: Both meet every stated requirement and handle the unsaid conditions soundly, so the difference is in what the operator and requester are given. Y tells the requester its behaviour in an accurate README and refuses bad data files and missing directories at startup, while Z tells nothing and silently overwrites a groups-less file (D-1). Y's larger test suite partly pins its own internals and misses the split check, so its edge is modest and closable in one short task.

pairs.why: Both build every stated requirement and handle every probed unsaid condition soundly. X adds an accurate README, refuses a groups-less or misplaced DATA_FILE, and its spec marks its own decisions, where Z tells the requester nothing and can silently overwrite a data file (D-1). Z's simpler number handling and write-failure test are real but smaller, and the gap is a short follow-up task.

Tests also exercise failed ledger writes and reopening a saved ledger, though by monkeypatching rename and hand-writing Y's own layout
Its tests catch removal of the unknown-split check; Y's suite passes with that check deleted
Smaller, cleaner maintenance surface: no shipped acceptance scripts, no spec with stale Open points and duplicated headings, fewer tests pinning internals

pairs.why: X and Y behave identically on every stated requirement, every unsaid probe and both defects, and both document their behaviour in near-identical READMEs. Y's id-length guard and failed-write tests are offset by its untested split check, stale spec and extra material a maintainer must carry. Neither gives the person running it anything that matters which the other lacks.
